summary: The hal-manifests group is 62 VINTF XML files, all of them the only etc/vintf files on the mounted partitions: vendor_a 20, odm_a 18, system_ext_a 12, system_a 11, product_a 1. None is a binary, library or firmware image. The files declare HAL package, version, transport and instance for the framework (system_a manifest.xml, level-based compatibility matrices 3 to 6 and a device matrix), system_ext, vendor and odm layers. Most declared HALs are also named in init service entries and in the SELinux hwservice_contexts or service_contexts files. A name-level cross-reference matched 414 manifest and matrix entries to context files; 7 matrix requirement names had no context entry. Two device-matrix requirements (vendor.oculus.hardware.mixedreality and vendor.oculus.hardware.peripheralconfig@1.0, both optional) have no provider among the 62 files. For two odm HALs (sensors and usb) the init rc or the hwservice context declares more interfaces or versions than the manifest fragment does.

claims.claim: The group has 62 rows, and these are exactly the 62 etc/vintf files present on the mounted partitions. Per partition: vendor_a 20, odm_a 18, system_ext_a 12, system_a 11, product_a 1. No other partition (odm_dlkm_a, vendor_dlkm_a, scratch) has a vintf file.

claims.evidence: cd <image>/mnt && find . -path '*etc/vintf*' -type f | sed 's|^\./||' | awk -F/ '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -c ; excerpt: '18 odm_a / 1 product_a / 11 system_a / 12 system_ext_a / 20 vendor_a'. Then: find . -path '*etc/vintf*' -type f | sed 's|^\./||' | sort > mounted_vintf.txt; awk -F'\t' '$1=="hal-manifests"{print $2"/"$3}' classified.tsv | sort > group_paths.txt; comm -23 mounted_vintf.txt group_paths.txt; comm -13 mounted_vintf.txt group_paths.txt; excerpt: 'mounted vintf files: 62 / in group: 62' and both comm outputs empty.
claims.reason: find under the mount for paths matching etc/vintf gives 62 files; sort then uniq -c per partition: odm_a 18, product_a 1, system_a 11, system_ext_a 12, vendor_a 20. Sorted mounted paths compared with the sorted partition/path rows of the group using comm: no lines in either direction (62 each). odm_dlkm_a, vendor_dlkm_a and scratch each have 0 vintf paths. Three further paths match the vintf pattern but are shared libraries, not etc/vintf files: system_a/system/lib/libvintf.so, system_a/system/lib64/libvintf.so, system_a/system/lib64/libkeystore2_vintf_cpp.so.

claims.claim: The compatibility matrices contain hidl and aidl requirements with optional true or false. Most requirements are optional (268 of 385 hal attributes are optional true). The device matrix has only optional entries.

claims.evidence: python census (see GRP-03): 'optional attr on <hal>: {'(unset)': 79, 'false': 38, 'true': 268}'. Device matrix check: python iterates compatibility_matrix.device.xml hal elements and prints optional values. Every hal entry in the device matrix shows optional="true" in the sed excerpt for 'vendor.oculus.hardware.peripheralconfig' (<hal format="hidl" optional="true">).
claims.reason: Split by root type: the 87 manifest hal elements have 8 optional true and 79 unset; the 298 compatibility-matrix hal elements have 260 optional true and 38 optional false, none unset. The 268 figure therefore mixes manifest and matrix entries, and the matrix-only count is 260 of 298. The file named compatibility_matrix.device.xml (root type framework) has 30 of 30 optional true, so the statement holds for that file. The device-type matrix, vendor_a/etc/vintf/compatibility_matrix.xml (root type device), has 6 of 6 optional false, so the device matrix does not have only optional entries. Matrix formats are hidl 261 and aidl 37, with optional values true or false in both.
claims.corrected_claim: The compatibility matrices contain hidl (261) and aidl (37) requirements. Of the 298 matrix requirement entries, 260 are optional true and 38 optional false. Across all 385 hal elements in the 62 files, 268 are optional true, 38 false and 79 have no attribute (the last two groups include manifest entries). The framework matrix compatibility_matrix.device.xml has 30 of 30 entries optional true; the device-type matrix vendor_a/etc/vintf/compatibility_matrix.xml has 6 of 6 entries optional false.

gaps: No binaries, libraries or firmware are in the group (all 62 rows are VINTF XML). Binaries named by init were checked only for existence and size, not analysed (no ELF dependency or symbol review).
HIDL .hal and AIDL interface sources are not on the mount. Method signatures, data types and version compatibility beyond the declared version numbers were not determined.
Kernel config inputs named in compatibility matrix headers (matrix_kernel_config_*.xml) are absent, so kernel requirement lines could not be matched to a kernel config.

Name-level coverage counts use only the 62 group manifests. No other manifest exists on the mounted partitions, so vendor.oculus.hardware.mixedreality and vendor.oculus.hardware.peripheralconfig have no provider on the mount. Whether a provider exists on a device image outside the mount is not determined.
Cross-reference is by name and instance only. hwservice_contexts entries carry no version, so version-level matching against the declared versions was not performed.
The SELinux policy compiled files (plat_pub_versioned.cil, vendor_sepolicy.cil) were searched for name matches only. Domain allow rules for each HAL were not analysed.
The init rc files for the vendor, system and product HAL services were read only where they name a group HAL. Services not tied to a group HAL, such as ovr_crashuploader.rc, were not read.

Version mismatches between init interface lines and manifests were recorded for usb (init lists 1.0 to 1.2, manifest 1.2 only) and perfservice (init lists IPower 1.0 to 1.3, manifest 1.3 only). Whether these mismatches affect runtime behaviour was not tested.

The sensors context file lists 18 interfaces for the vendor.oculus.hardware.sensors package, the odm manifest 10. The runtime registry contents were not observed, so it is not known which interfaces the sensor service actually registers.
Runtime behaviour (service start, registration with hwservicemanager or servicemanager, VINTF check at boot) was not observed. All statements about it are from file content only.
file(1) labels for these XML files are inconsistent (XML document versus exported SGML document). The file-type labels were not used as evidence beyond recording that inconsistency.
